10_marg327: Rabanus. Some understand him as the decalogue, and his wife as the Synagogue, and the two sons as the royal and the priestly honour, which won themselves a union not only in the nation of the Jews but also of the proselytes, as was done in the time of David and Solomon and others.

Whence: “Give you them to eat.” Again: “Going, preach the gospel of the kingdom of God.” And elsewhere: “I have chosen you out of the world, that you should go, and should bring forth fruit.”

10_interl535: in Christ, or in his commandments
10_marg333: The Church does not act without discernment, nor receive anyone without discernment; whence: Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits if they be of God. 10_marg334: Rabanus. The voice of the Synagogue confessing the truth and not keeping silent about the guilt that has come upon her, who, forsaken by her husband, that is, David, and deprived of her sons, that is, kings and princes, confesses that after the coming of Christ she is barren and too weak to conceive sons to God.
10_interl538: elsewhere: my daughters, and go your ways
10_marg335: By these women, one of whom, grieving and mourning, departs from her mother in law, while the other clings to her with a steadfast mind, believers are signified: some of whom, having received the grace of baptism and the fellowship of faith, fall back into their former errors, whom Orpha signifies, who went back to her gods; but others, with settled purpose, keep the grace they have received, whom Ruth signifies.
10_marg336: So the Church called from the Gentiles, leaving her country, that is, abandoning idolatry, fleshly life and desires, professes that her God is he in whom the saints believed, and that she will go where the flesh of Christ ascended, and suffer for his name in this world even unto death, and be with the people of the saints and prophets and patriarchs; whence: “Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.”
10_marg337: Noemi, seeing, and so on. The Gentile people follows the preachers with steadfast mind into the holy land and into Bethlehem, the city of God, where it is prepared to receive the bridegroom born of the stock of Abraham, in whom all nations or tribes of the earth shall be blessed.
10_marg338: Call me not, and so on. The Synagogue acknowledges her calamity, which she deservedly suffers after the coming of Christ, and shrinks from being called beautiful, because she sees the times of her prosperity ending.
10_marg339: In the beginning of the barley harvest, and so on. That is, when it turns the order of his incarnation to the mystery of Christ’s passion. For the barley harvest expresses the time of the Lord’s passion, which fell in the month of new corn, that is, in the first month. Rightly then they come to Bethlehem at that time, when the law preaches that Christ, whom it teaches was born in Bethlehem, was slain at the pasch, that is, in the month of new corn. Holy Church too labours with all her strength to steep those whom she calls to the faith in the merit of the incarnation, passion and resurrection. The barley harvest expresses the believing of the Jews, who, the sacrament of the passion being accomplished, came first to the faith at the apostles’ preaching; who elsewhere are read to have been fed by the Lord with five barley loaves.
10_interl539: “The strength of God”; whence: “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Prince of Peace, the Father of the world to come.”
10_marg340: This man, the kinsman of Elimelech, is Christ, the lamb of the law and the lawgiver, because he was promised through the law and born of the patriarchs, and of the nation of the Jews according to the flesh. Whence: “God will raise up to you a prophet of your brethren; him you shall hear as myself.” He is the powerful one who vanquished the prince of the world and subdued the whole world to his rule; and very rich, because he is “possessor of heaven and earth”, and “in him are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge”. For he is “the power of God and the wisdom”.
10_interl541: The ears left behind signify the faithful who, the rest having been taken up to heaven, are left to us as an example
10_interl542: The harvest is the saints, who are gathered to be laid up in God’s barn. The reapers are the angels.
10_marg341: And it happened, and so on. Because holy Church belongs to Christ, whose bride and body she is; of whom it is said: “The Lord is my strength and my praise.” And elsewhere: “The Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.” He is the kinsman of Elimelech, who, born of Bethlehem and of the stock of David, has witness from the law and the prophets. He brought the words of salvation to his household; at his birth the angels sang: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will. When he came into Jerusalem, the crowd met him, crying out: “Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.”
10_interl543: because Christ, as if not knowing, asks about the faith of the Gentiles of any of the teachers who is set over the lesser priests, when he stirs him up to preach
10_interl544: because from the beginning, that is, of faith, to the perfection of good work
10_marg342: And she desired leave, and so on. Because holy Church perseveres in the field of divine reading after the reapers and preachers, gathering the mysteries of the Scriptures, so as to store the testimonies and examples of the virtues in the bosom of her mind. Or that field is the discipline of heavenly study; the harvest, spiritual understanding; the reapers, the preachers; the ears left behind, the sentences of the Scriptures, which, being much hidden in mystery, remain as it were fuller, for the exercise of one who meditates. So the Gentile people ardently longs for the Church’s discipline, that it may be admitted to the meditation of the divine law and the fellowship of the saints, and be refreshed by the teachings or examples of the saints.
10_marg343: As if to say: Do not depart from the state of faith, do not follow the errors of heretics or schismatics, but rather join thyself to holy souls, that thou mayest reap the holy Scriptures by meditating and fulfilling them in deed, and mayest drink the draught of divine wisdom from the books of the two Testaments, whence the young men, that is, the saints, drink.
10_marg344: The Church of the Gentiles gives thanks to the Saviour, who has deigned to regard her. He answers her that it pleases him that, her husband, that is, the devil, being dead, she has left her idolatrous parents and the land of her birth, that is, fleshly desires, and has joined herself to the people of the saints, which was unknown to her before, when she followed the lust of the old man.
10_interl546: that is, by faith; whence: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he hath sent.”
10_interl547: the two Testaments, with which God protects those who flee to him; whence: “In the shadow of thy wings will I hope.”
10_marg345: I have found, and so on. Note the humility of the Church of the Gentiles, which knows herself unequal to so great a grace, and does not dare to make herself equal to the first Church. Whence she says: “For the whelps also eat of the crumbs that fall from the table of their masters.” And elsewhere: “Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed”, and so on.
10_marg346: The hour of eating was when it was said to the apostles: “Going, teach ye all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.” For it had been said by the Lord: “Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles.”
10_marg347: Dip thy morsel, and so on. In the law, that is, which, so long as it was meditated upon, persevering in the former people, corrupted by the conditions or traditions of the Pharisees, lost its native savour. In this the Church dips her morsel, that is, she learns that the mysteries of Christ’s incarnation are in the Old Testament; and so she believes the more firmly, because she knows it was prefigured long before.
10_interl548: because the Gentile Church joins herself to the holy preachers through faith

10_interl550: because she chewed over each word that she heard with fine discernment
10_interl551: because she kept the words she had heard in her heart, and laboured earnestly in meditating, that she might take in greater things
10_marg348: Note the humility of the householder, who not only lets the ears of the testimonies that are left be gathered, but also bestows handfuls of knowledge with unasked largess.
10_marg349: Some of your handfuls, and so on. Because he does not despise the weakness of the Gentile people, nor reproach it with its former errors, but by the shrewdness of his care leads it on to edification.

10_interl575: he asks for the Church’s confession
10_interl576: The Church desires above all things the grace of faith and of Christ’s protection.

10_interl578: because after thou camest to Christ thou hast steadfastly persevered
10_interl579: heretics or schismatics, who have no ripeness of counsel, because they are always unstable and uncertain
10_interl580: “Ask, and you shall receive”; “Seek, and you shall find.” Whatever faith rightly asks, the kindness of Christ grants.

10_marg367: Because Christ saw the law set up bodily for the Jews, and bade it turn aside to him, because he bent it to bear witness to the mystery of his dispensation. 10_interl593: the fathers of the Old Testament, that is, those who kept the decalogue, and knew that Christ’s incarnation was foreshadowed there
10_marg368: Fittingly he offered the part of Noemi’s field to the lawyer to buy, when he showed the masters of the Synagogue the part of the people that remained to be saved, grace having now appeared, that they might acknowledge their weakness, and commit what they themselves could not do to the true physician to be done; whence it is said to the lepers: Go, show yourselves to the priests; and as they went, they were made clean.
10_marg369: He signifies no other possession of the people than the joining of the Church in marriage to Christ, who raised up the ancient name of sons of God, which the saints had at the beginning. Whence: “The sons of God seeing”, and so on; and Luke says: “Adam, who was of God”; which name he raised up in the Church of the Gentiles by the grace of God. Whence: “He gave them power to be made the sons of God”, and so on. This name the decalogue of the law could not raise up among the nations. But if thou refer this to John the Baptist, thou wilt find him yielding his right of kinship and saying: “I baptize with water; but there hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to loose.” And elsewhere: “I am not Christ, but … I am sent before him. He that hath the bride is the bridegroom.” The law too yields to the Gospel. For the law entered in, that sin might abound, grace abounding more. There is indeed a setting aside of the former commandment, because of its weakness; but a bringing in of a better hope, by which we draw nigh to God, through Jesus Christ.
10_marg370: Put off his shoe, and so on. The shoe is the veil of the mysteries. The law took off the shoe from its foot and gave it to Christ, because it could not make the sacraments plain through the masters of the people, but kept this to be done by Christ. So John claimed the shoe not for himself but for Christ, because he understood that the bride belonged to Christ alone; whence he says: “I am not worthy to loose the latchet of his shoe.”
10_marg371: So Christ has witnesses enough from both Testaments, that the people of the Gentiles, which the decalogue, now ended, could not make fruitful spiritually, he himself made fruitful with the seed of the word, possessing all that the earlier and later saints had.
10_marg372: And the ancients, and so on. Isidore. The blessing of the ten ancients shows that all nations are to be blessed in the name of Jesus. For iota, which is the first letter in the name of Jesus, signifies ten among the Greeks.
10_marg373: They pray for prosperity for the Church of the Gentiles, that she may receive the grace of fruitfulness that the first parents of the Israelites had.
10_marg374: The beauty of inward contemplation, having inward understanding of the truth. Whence Rachel, “well favoured and of a beautiful countenance”, whom every devoutly zealous man loves and for whom he serves Laban, who is interpreted “whitening”, which he compares to the grace of God, who says: “If your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made as white as snow.”
10_marg375: The action of this life in which we live is laborious, from faith, and uncertain as to the outcome by which it will come to the profit of those whom we wish to help. This is Lia, the first wife of Jacob, who is recorded to have had weak eyes.
10_marg376: Phares, and so on. Because the Gentile people held the grace, and in the birth went before the brother who had first put out his hand. For Israel first put out its hand in the work of the law, and drew it back defiled with the blood of the prophets and of Christ himself. But afterwards the people of the Gentiles broke forth, that “the first should be last, and the last first”. Thamar too is interpreted “changing” or “bitterness”. For the Church of the Gentiles, both in name and in bearing, which was foul and bitter in idolatry, becomes sweet and beautiful in penance.
10_interl594: because the Church joined to Christ bears spiritual offspring; whence: “The barren hath borne many: and she that had many children is weakened.”
10_marg377: The Church is always made fruitful by the gift of the Holy Spirit, and as some depart to everlasting light others will succeed, so that the Christian name may remain for ever, and the most holy mother may have comfort from new offspring in her old age. As the patriarchs and prophets departed, too, the evangelists and apostles succeeded them. Whence: “Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee.”
10_marg378: The daughter in law of the Synagogue is the Gentile Church, which married Christ, born of the Synagogue. Him, namely, she could not bring forth through the law; received through the mystery of prophecy, she carried him hidden, figured under a veil, and performed the office of a nurse, because she lacked the privilege of a mother.
10_marg379: That is, than the multitude of those who were nourished in the Old Testament by the teaching of the law, who, namely, did not believe the word of the Lord, “and they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to devils”, and at last killed Christ and persecuted the apostles.
10_marg380: The spiritual lineage of the generation is shown. For Obed is interpreted “serving”; Isai, “sacrifice in the sun”, or “incense”; David, “strong of hand”, or “desirable”. For he who serves God earnestly offers him a pleasing sacrifice and incense of sweetest odour through works of virtue and zeal in prayer; and so, strengthened by faith and devotion, he is desirable and pleases God.
10_marg381: The powers of heaven, which rejoice in the fruitfulness of the Church, and call his name Obed, that is, serving, whom they desire to serve the King on high with them.
10_marg382: There are ten generations from Juda’s son to David. From which thou knowest that the purpose of the whole divine law tends to Christ, who was born of the seed of David, to proclaim his coming and to show the perfection of the law in him: “For the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to every one that believeth.” So before the law Jacob says of Christ’s incarnation: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and so on. And to David, because Christ is of the seed of Juda, it was said: Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne. It is plain, then, that the oracle of all the prophets and patriarchs belongs to the dispensation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
